questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the terms:

(i) Economic growth. (4 marks)

(ii) Economic development. (4 marks)

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Economic growth (4 marks)**

**Economic growth** is a **sustained increase in the real output of goods and services** (real national income or real GDP) of a country over a period of time, usually a year. It is measured by the **percentage change in real GDP**, and is a **quantitative** change: the economy produces more.

*Example:* if real output rises from 10 000 million to 10 400 million FCFA, growth is $\dfrac{400}{10\,000} \times 100 = 4\%$ (hypothetical figures).

**(ii) Economic development (4 marks)**

**Economic development** is a **sustained improvement in the standard of living and quality of life of the population**, accompanied by **changes in the structure of the economy**. It includes growth of national income and also **better education, health, housing, life expectancy and lower poverty and inequality**, with more industry and services and less dependence on primary production. It is a **qualitative** as well as a quantitative change.

*Difference:* growth is about **more output**, development is about **better living conditions** for all. A country can grow without developing if the gains go only to a few people.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain four benefits of economic growth.

(12 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** **Economic growth** means a rise in real national output over time. It brings the following benefits to a country.

**1. Higher incomes and a better standard of living.** More output means more goods and services per person, if growth is faster than population growth. People can afford more food, better housing, health care and education, and enjoy a higher **standard of living**.

**2. More employment and lower poverty.** Growing industries, farms and services **need more workers**, so jobs are created, unemployment falls and incomes rise for poor families, which reduces poverty.

**3. Higher government revenue and better public services.** When incomes and profits increase, the government collects **more taxes** (income tax, company tax, VAT) without raising tax rates. It can use the extra revenue to build **roads, schools, hospitals and water supplies**, and to pay its debts.

**4. Improvement in the balance of payments and in investment.** A growing economy can produce **more goods for export** (and substitutes for imports), so foreign exchange earnings rise and the balance of payments improves. Rising profits and incomes also provide **savings and investment**, and attract foreign investors, which further helps growth.

**Other benefits:** better infrastructure, more choice for consumers and the ability to protect the environment and finance research.

**Conclusion.** Economic growth raises living standards, creates jobs and strengthens the government's finances, although its benefits should be shared fairly and it must not damage the environment.
